correctness.rationale: The invariant polygon reduction follows by the exact reciprocal-spacing identity. Direct holomorphic differentiation gives a circulant whose off-diagonal Fourier transforms differ by an explicit quadratic integer factor. The radial Fourier eigenvalue is the exact derivative of the scalar map; all other eigenvalues follow from a finite root-of-unity sum recurrence. Strict coefficient ordering establishes the Euclidean norm and its sharp transition. Two polynomial identities with positive coefficients prove global no-overshoot radial convergence; local vanishing Jacobian and continuity give the open convergence basin. The 852 standalone finite checks are supporting consistency checks, not the proof of all degrees.

value.rationale: The naturally used equally spaced start configurations reduce to a convergent one-dimensional invariant family, but full ambient perturbations can initially expand. The exact normal-mode spectrum for every degree identifies the worst perturbation direction and the unique sharp boundary between expansion and contraction. This is a structural numerical stability benchmark not supplied by standard local cubic convergence, a mere renaming, or a finite parameter experiment.
